entries.not_relevant_because: The family's only manuscript, 'The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture', proves that for one fixed real shift γ and a weight ψ, almost every real x satisfies ‖qx−γ‖ < ψ(q) for infinitely many q whenever Σ φ(q)ψ(q)/q diverges. It is a one-variable, inhomogeneous, weighted statement about a single real number. It says nothing about a pair of reals α, β, about the product n‖nα‖‖nβ‖, or about its liminf being 0. The word 'Littlewood' appears in the text only in the bibliography title of Chow–Technau (references/main.bib), which is cited for the weak conjecture, not for Littlewood.
